public_rationale: The evidence shows useful co-writing and a watchable generated television imitation. Neither establishes that AI could independently replace a professional screenwriter or room. Equally, collaborative workflows and the absence of documented studio replacement do not prove inability. The ordinary professional-replacement reading remains unsettled.
limitations: Professional usability has no specified threshold.
The available demonstration is narrower than a writer's full role.
The professional co-writing study predates the target period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: As of August 2023, AI cannot realistically replace a writer or a writers' room.

statement.excerpt: AI isn’t currently at a place (nor do I believe it will be for some time) where it could realistically replace a writer or writer’s room

our_interpretation: The Hollywood strike context makes professional screenwriting the relevant work.
Realistic replacement means delivering usable professional writing without substantial human writing or rewriting. Ordinary direction and editorial feedback remain permissible.
Generating dialogue or assisting a writer is relevant but does not by itself establish replacement.
For this ongoing capability claim, I use July 2023, the latest complete month before publication, as the reporting period.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evaluations or documented production experience show that available systems could not perform the substantive work of a professional screenwriter or writers' room without substantial human writing.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented production or credible professional evaluation demonstrates that AI could perform that work to usable standards without substantial human writing.
